questions.q: In which water body are the Andaman and Nicobar Islands located?
questions.a: They are located in the Bay of Bengal. A wrong answer here suggests the student has not yet learned to distinguish between the two major water bodies flanking the Indian peninsula.

questions.q: Why is an island not considered a continent?
questions.a: An island is much smaller than a continent; while both are surrounded by water, continents are massive, continuous landmasses. A wrong answer shows confusion about the scale of landforms.

questions.q: If you were traveling from Mumbai to the Lakshadweep Islands, which sea would you be crossing?
questions.a: You would be crossing the Arabian Sea. A wrong answer indicates the student is not yet connecting the physical location of islands to the neighboring seas on the Indian map.

questions.q: Compare the Andaman and Nicobar Islands with a typical small island. What makes the Andaman group unique based on the provided text?
questions.a: The Andaman group consists of over 500 islands and is mountainous with dense forests, whereas many other islands are smaller or flatter. A wrong answer suggests the student failed to notice the descriptive details provided about this specific island chain.

questions.q: Could a landmass that is only 5 kilometers wide and surrounded by water be called a continent? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, it would be called an island because "continent" refers to massive, continuous landmasses, not small isolated pieces of land. A wrong answer reveals a failure to grasp the scale difference between continents and islands.

questions.q: Imagine you discover a new, tiny, uninhabited island in the Indian Ocean. How would you explain to a friend why it is an island and not a continent?
questions.a: I would explain that because it is small and completely surrounded by water, it fits the definition of an island rather than a massive continent. A poor answer would fail to mention the key criteria of size or the surrounding water.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: An island is a piece of land that is smaller than a continent and is ______ surrounded by water on all sides.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever seen a small sandcastle ______ by water in a puddle after the rain?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to correctly identify the location of India’s two island groups on a map and describe one key geographical difference between them.
